title: HELIX Terminology: Worker Type
description: Classification of institutional workers by employment relationship.

codes.definition: Permanent employee on the institutional payroll with benefits eligibility. Includes both full-time and part-time regular appointments.
Employee hired for a defined period, typically not to exceed 12 months. May or may not be benefits-eligible depending on FTE and institutional policy.
Individual engaged through a staffing agency or third-party arrangement. Not on the institutional payroll; paid through accounts payable.
Individual providing services under a contract (1099). Must meet IRS independent contractor tests. Not an employee for benefits, tax withholding, or FLSA purposes.

Currently enrolled student employed by the institution. Includes Federal Work-Study (FWS), institutional employment, and hourly student positions. Typically exempt from FICA if enrolled half-time or more.

Graduate student holding a funded assistantship (GA, TA, RA). Typically receives tuition remission plus stipend. May be classified as student or employee depending on state law and collective bargaining status.

Individual in a structured learning experience, paid or unpaid. Unpaid internships at for-profit entities must meet DOL primary beneficiary test; universities have more flexibility under educational exception.

Individual receiving a fellowship (external or institutional) for research or scholarly activity. May not have an employment relationship; fellowship stipends are often non-compensatory and reported on 1099-MISC or 1042-S.
Individual providing services without expectation of compensation. Must meet FLSA volunteer criteria. Cannot volunteer in roles identical to their paid position at the same institution.
Retired faculty or staff member granted emeritus status by the governing board. May retain certain privileges (email, library, office) but is not actively employed or compensated unless rehired.
Individual holding a doctoral degree engaged in supervised research training. Classified as employee or trainee depending on funding source (NIH NRSA = trainee, institutional funds = employee).

Part-time faculty hired on a per-course or per-term basis without tenure eligibility. Typically compensated per credit hour or per course. May be subject to ACA hour tracking for benefits eligibility.
